methodological_rigor.justification: Small descriptive case series (n=12 patients, 26 tissue samples). No control group or comparative statistical analysis. Morphometry manual and subjective despite quality-control measures (Bland-Altman concordance only 0.14 µm² difference between replicates, which is not negligible relative to measured differences). No power calculation or a priori sample size justification. Statistical comparisons between recurrent/non-recurrent groups not detailed in text; appears largely descriptive. TMB analysis mentioned but integration with morphometry unclear.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Case series with long-term follow-up of recurrent chordoma (7-16 years). Chordoma is rare malignant tumor with high recurrence; study addresses prognostic question of interest. However, findings are observational only without predictive validation. No therapeutic recommendations or clinical decision-making framework provided. Potential future utility depends on validation in larger cohorts.

reporting_quality.justification: Histopathological methods clear; immunohistochemistry protocols detailed. ARRIVE adherence partial (study population defined; methods described; but no protocol registration, no statement of data availability, no code/software accessibility mentioned). Manual morphometry inherently difficult to reproduce without original digital images and detailed annotation guidelines. Whole-exome sequencing methods sparse (data location, analysis pipeline, variant calling parameters not specified).

novelty_literature.justification: Novel application of quantitative nuclear morphometry to chordoma recurrence prediction. Integration of morphometry with immunophenotype and genomic profiling (TMB) is methodologically interesting. However, findings are largely observational (pleomorphic changes, lamin A/C disruption) without mechanistic novelty. Limited by absence of independent validation cohort or external dataset testing.

writing_presentation.justification: Manuscript is clearly written with logical organization. Methods detailed and generally reproducible. Figures and tables communicate findings effectively, including clinical timeline and morphometric parameters. However, results section is largely descriptive without strong quantitative summary tables; statistical analyses and p-values sparse. Discussion appropriately contextualizes findings within broader morphometry and sarcoma literature but acknowledges study limitations.

key_strengths: Unique long-term follow-up of recurrent chordoma (7-16 years) with integrated morphometric, immunophenotypic, and genomic analysis
Quantitative nuclear morphometry measured objectively across large sample of nuclei (mean 317 per specimen), with internal quality control
Integration of multiple biomarker modalities (morphometry, IHC, WES) provides comprehensive characterization
Rare tumor with few prognostic studies; any systematic analysis contributes to knowledge base
key_concerns: Severely underpowered case series (n=12 patients) for generating generalizable conclusions; no statistical power analysis provided
Manual morphometry subjective despite quality control; reproducibility across observers not assessed
No validation cohort; single-center data from specialized bone tumor registry may not generalize
Morphometric differences between groups not clearly quantified with statistical testing; many findings presented qualitatively
chief_reviewer.rationale: Interesting morphometric case series with potential for future development, but current sample size (n=12) does not support conclusions about recurrence prediction or therapeutic utility. Appropriate for Tier 4 with major revisions: requires either larger prospective validation cohort or repositioning as hypothesis-generating preliminary work.
